body.statement:
Fix \(m\geq 1\) and \(0<\xi\leq a_m\), and let \(n\to\infty\). There exist constants \(0<c<C_0<\infty\), depending only on \(\delta_0\) and \(c_0\), such that
\[
 \sup_{h\in H_m(\xi)}P_{m,h}^{n}\!\left\{\exists (v,j):N_{v,j}=0\ \text{or}\ \widehat s_{v,j}\neq\operatorname{sign}(h_{v,j})\right\}
 \leq C_0m\exp\!\left(-\frac{cn\xi^2}{m}\right).
\]
Uniformly over \(h\in H_m(\xi)\),
\[
 \sqrt n
 \binom{\overline L_{n,m}-L_m(h)}{\overline U_{n,m}-U_m(h)}
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}
 \binom{8k\sum_{j=1}^{m}\operatorname{sign}(h_{0,j})\mathbf 1\{V_i=0,J_i=j,S_i=0,T_i=0\}(R_i-h_{0,j})}
 {-8k\sum_{j=1}^{m}\operatorname{sign}(h_{1,j})\mathbf 1\{V_i=1,J_i=j,S_i=0,T_i=1\}(R_i-h_{1,j})}
 +o_{P_{m,h}^{n}}(1),
\]
where the remainder is uniform in probability. The empirical variances are uniformly consistent in the sense that, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \sup_{h\in H_m(\xi)}P_{m,h}^{n}\!\left\{
 \left|\widehat\sigma_L^2-\frac{8k^2}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\{p_0(1-p_0)-h_{0,j}^2\}\right|
 +\left|\widehat\sigma_U^2-\frac{8k^2}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\{p_0(1-p_0)-h_{1,j}^2\}\right|>\varepsilon\right\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
After division by the respective square roots of the two displayed limiting variances, the endpoint-center vector converges uniformly to \(\mathcal N_2(0,I_2)\); in particular, its two coordinates are asymptotically independent. Consequently the signed-cell benchmark satisfies
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{h\in H_m(\xi)}P_{m,h}^{n}\{L_m(h)\in(C^{\mathrm{sign}}_{n,m})_L,\ U_m(h)\in(C^{\mathrm{sign}}_{n,m})_U\}\geq1-\delta_0.
\]
The coordinate-rectangle rule \(C^{\mathrm{rect}}_{n,m}\) in \(\mathrm{def:coordinate-rectangle-interval}\) is a finite-sample member of \(\mathcal I_{n,m}\) and obeys, for every \(h\in H_m\),
\[
 R_{n,m}(C^{\mathrm{rect}}_{n,m},h)\leq4kr_{n,m}.
\]
It follows, uniformly over \(h\in H_m(\xi)\) (indeed uniformly over \(H_m\)), that
\[
 \ell_{n,m}(h)\asymp_{m,\xi,\delta_0}n^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 \sup_{h\in H_m(\xi)}\frac{R_{n,m}(C^{\mathrm{rect}}_{n,m},h)}{\ell_{n,m}(h)}=O_{m,\xi,\delta_0}(1).
\]
The rule \(C^{\mathrm{sign}}_{n,m}\) is asserted here only to be an asymptotically valid regular benchmark, not a member of the finite-sample globally honest class.
body.justification: This proposition is the proved regular fixed-dimensional reduction: it combines a globally honest coordinate-rectangle oracle witness with the separated-profile asymptotic analysis of the signed-cell benchmark.
body.gap: The fixed-dimensional regular oracle and limiting benchmark are now closed. The sharp profile, sharp adaptation factor, and globally attaining family when the dimension varies remain exclusively in the full-profile open question.
body.consumer: It certifies conventional jointly calibrated endpoint inference when every active max/min comparison is separated, and supplies a finite-sample honest fallback whose fixed-dimensional length is oracle-order.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(A_{i,v,j}=\mathbf 1\{V_i=v,J_i=j,S_i=0,T_i=v\}\). By \(\mathrm{def:observed-law}\),
\[
 P_{m,h}(A_{i,v,j}=1)=\frac12\frac1m\frac12\frac12=\frac1{8m}.
\]
Conditional on \(A_{i,v,j}=1\) and \(Z_i=z\), the Bernoulli mean is \(p_0+zh_{v,j}\). Hence, using \(R_i=Z_i(B_i-p_0)\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{m,h}[R_i\mid A_{i,v,j}=1,Z_i=z]
 =z\{p_0+zh_{v,j}-p_0\}=h_{v,j}.
\]
It follows from the definition of \(W_{i,v,j}\) and the preceding cell probability that
\[
 \mathbb E_{m,h}W_{i,v,j}=8m\frac1{8m}h_{v,j}=h_{v,j}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Because \(p_0=13/22\), the support of \(R_i\) is contained in \([-13/22,13/22]\). Thus \(W_{i,v,j}\) is contained in an interval of length \(104m/11<16m\).

We record the bounded-mean inequality used below and derive it here. If independent random variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are each supported on an interval of length at most \(d\), then, for every \(t\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 \mathbb E\exp\{t(X_i-\mathbb EX_i)\}\leq\exp(t^2d^2/8).
\]
Indeed, the second derivative of the centered log moment-generating function is the variance under an exponentially tilted law. Every law supported on an interval of length \(d\) has variance at most \(d^2/4\), because its variance is no larger than its mean squared distance from the interval midpoint. Integrating the second-derivative bound twice from zero proves the display. Markov's inequality, independence, and optimization at \(t=4x/d^2\) therefore give
\[
 P\!\left(\left|n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(X_i-\mathbb EX_i)\right|\geq x\right)
 \leq2\exp(-2nx^2/d^2).                                                  \tag{2}
\]
Applying (2) to (1), with \(d=16m\) and \(x=r_{n,m}\), yields
\[
 P_{m,h}^{n}(|\overline W_{v,j}-h_{v,j}|>r_{n,m})
 \leq2\exp\{-nr_{n,m}^2/(128m^2)\}
 =\frac{\delta_0}{2m}.                                                    \tag{3}
\]
The scalar projection onto \([-a_m,a_m]\) is nonexpansive and \(h_{v,j}\in[-a_m,a_m]\), so (3) implies \(|\widetilde h_{v,j}-h_{v,j}|\leq r_{n,m}\) on the same event. A union bound over the \(2m\) coordinates gives
\[
 P_{m,h}^{n}\{h_{v,j}\in I_{v,j}\text{ for every }(v,j)\}\geq1-\delta_0.       \tag{4}
\]
This bound is uniform over the entire cube \(H_m\), including its boundary.

For fixed \(v\), the map \((g_{v,1},\ldots,g_{v,m})\mapsto m^{-1}\sum_j|g_{v,j}|\) is continuous, and its domain \(\prod_jI_{v,j}\) is compact and connected. Its image is consequently a compact interval. Separability of the sum shows that its endpoints are exactly those displayed in \(D_v\). On the event in (4), \(T_v(h)\in D_v\) for both \(v\). By \(\mathrm{def:endpoints}\), this implies simultaneously
\[
 L_m(h)=-b+kT_0(h)\in-b+kD_0,
 \qquad
 U_m(h)=b-kT_1(h)\in b-kD_1.                                               \tag{5}
\]
Moreover, the map \(x\mapsto|x|\) is one-Lipschitz, so the range of \(|x|\) on each \(I_{v,j}\) has length at most \(\operatorname{length}(I_{v,j})\leq2r_{n,m}\). Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{length}(D_v)\leq\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^{m}2r_{n,m}=2r_{n,m}.          \tag{6}
\]
The construction is a measurable pair of closed intervals, and \(D_v\subseteq[0,a_m]\), so its endpoint images satisfy the required range projection. Equations (4)--(5) give joint coverage at least \(1-\delta_0\). Hence \(C^{\mathrm{rect}}_{n,m}\in\mathcal I_{n,m}\) by \(\mathrm{def:honest-class}\). Equation (6) gives the deterministic length bound
\[
 R_{n,m}(C^{\mathrm{rect}}_{n,m},h)
 \leq k\{\operatorname{length}(D_0)+\operatorname{length}(D_1)\}
 \leq4kr_{n,m}.                                                           \tag{7}
\]

Since the local oracle is an infimum over \(\mathcal I_{n,m}\), (7) is an upper bound for \(\ell_{n,m}(h)\). By \(\mathrm{thm:oracle-positivity}\), after possibly decreasing \(c\),
\[
 ck\min\{a_m,n^{-1/2}\}\leq\ell_{n,m}(h)
 \leq4km\sqrt{128\log(4m/\delta_0)}\,n^{-1/2}.                             \tag{8}
\]
For fixed \(m\), \(a_m>0\), and hence the minimum on the left of (8) equals \(n^{-1/2}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). This proves \(\ell_{n,m}(h)\asymp_{m,\delta_0}n^{-1/2}\) uniformly over \(H_m\), and therefore over \(H_m(\xi)\). Dividing (7) by the left side of (8) proves the asserted fixed-dimensional oracle-ratio corollary. Notice that its constant depends on \(m\); thus (8) says nothing about the sharp simultaneous order when \(m\) varies.

It remains to establish the regular benchmark assertions. For a fixed cell, \(N_{v,j}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,1/(8m))\), independently of \(h\). Conditional on \(N_{v,j}=q>0\), the selected \(R_i\)'s are independent, have mean \(h_{v,j}\), and lie in an interval of length \(13/11\). If \(|h_{v,j}|\geq\xi\), a sign error implies that the selected mean differs from \(h_{v,j}\) by at least \(\xi\). Thus (2) gives, for \(\lambda=2(11/13)^2\xi^2\),
\[
 P_{m,h}^{n}\{\widehat s_{v,j}\neq\operatorname{sign}(h_{v,j})\mid N_{v,j}=q\}
 \leq2e^{-\lambda q}.                                                      \tag{9}
\]
The same right side, enlarged by the empty-cell event, is bounded by three times the binomial Laplace transform. Since
\[
 \mathbb E e^{-\lambda N_{v,j}}
 =\left(1-\frac1{8m}+\frac{e^{-\lambda}}{8m}\right)^n
 \leq\exp\!\left\{-\frac{n(1-e^{-\lambda})}{8m}\right\},                 \tag{10}
\]
and \(\xi\leq a_m\leq1/32\) implies \(1-e^{-\lambda}\geq\lambda/2\), a union bound in (9)--(10) over \(2m\) cells proves the stated uniform exponential sign-recovery inequality, after enlarging \(C_0\) and decreasing \(c\).

For the linear expansion, write
\[
 S_{v,j}=\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_{i,v,j}(R_i-h_{v,j}),
 \qquad q_n=\frac{n}{8m}.
\]
On the event of no empty cell and correct sign recovery, \(\widehat s_{v,j}=\operatorname{sign}(h_{v,j})\) and
\[
 \overline h_{v,j}-h_{v,j}=\frac{S_{v,j}}{N_{v,j}}.
\]
For fixed \(m\), the bounded-mean argument (2), applied to the counts and the centered cell sums, gives, uniformly in \(h\in H_m(\xi)\),
\[
 \max_{v,j}|N_{v,j}-q_n|=O_{P_{m,h}^{n}}(\sqrt n),
 \qquad
 \max_{v,j}|S_{v,j}|=O_{P_{m,h}^{n}}(\sqrt n),                              \tag{11}
\]
and the probability that some \(N_{v,j}<q_n/2\) tends to zero exponentially. On the complementary event,
\[
 \left|\frac1{N_{v,j}}-\frac1{q_n}\right|
 \leq\frac{2|N_{v,j}-q_n|}{q_n^2}=O_{P_{m,h}^{n}}(n^{-3/2})                 \tag{12}
\]
uniformly. Combining (11)--(12), summing over the fixed number \(m\) of cells, and using the exponential sign bound shows that replacing every \(N_{v,j}^{-1}\) by \(q_n^{-1}=8m/n\) contributes \(o_{P_{m,h}^{n}}(n^{-1/2})\) to either endpoint center, uniformly over \(H_m(\xi)\). The endpoint formulas in \(\mathrm{def:endpoints}\) and the centers in \(\mathrm{def:signed-cell-mean-interval}\) now give exactly the asserted two-dimensional asymptotic linear expansion.

We next compute its covariance rather than assume it. Conditional on the informative cell and after averaging over \(Z_i\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{m,h}R_i^2
 =\frac12\sum_{z\in\{-1,1\}}\left[(p_0+zh_{v,j})(1-p_0)^2+(1-p_0-zh_{v,j})p_0^2\right]
 =p_0(1-p_0).
\]
Together with \(\mathbb E R_i=h_{v,j}\), this yields
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{m,h}(R_i\mid A_{i,v,j}=1)=p_0(1-p_0)-h_{v,j}^2.          \tag{13}
\]
The cell indicators are disjoint. Therefore the variances of the lower and upper leading summands are respectively
\[
 \frac{8k^2}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\{p_0(1-p_0)-h_{0,j}^2\},
 \qquad
 \frac{8k^2}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\{p_0(1-p_0)-h_{1,j}^2\},                     \tag{14}
\]
and their cross-covariance is zero because their product vanishes identically when \(V_i\) cannot equal both zero and one. Since \(p_0=13/22\) and \(a_m\leq1/32\), both quantities in (14) are bounded above and bounded away from zero uniformly in \(h\).

By the definition of the empirical influence scores, disjointness of the cell indicators removes all cross-products and the estimated signs disappear after squaring. For example,
\[
 \widehat\sigma_L^2
 =\frac{64k^2}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_{i,0,j}(R_i-\overline h_{0,j})^2. \tag{15}
\]
The within-cell identity
\[
 \sum_iA_{i,v,j}(R_i-\overline h_{v,j})^2
 =\sum_iA_{i,v,j}(R_i-h_{v,j})^2-N_{v,j}(\overline h_{v,j}-h_{v,j})^2       \tag{16}
\]
holds whenever the cell is nonempty. The last term in (16), divided by \(n\), is \(o_{P_{m,h}^{n}}(1)\) uniformly by (11)--(12); empty cells have exponentially vanishing probability. Applying the bounded-mean inequality to the finite collection of empirical moments on the right of (16), and using (13), proves that (15) converges uniformly to the first quantity in (14). The upper endpoint is identical with \(v=1\), proving the displayed variance-consistency assertion.

Finally, standardize the leading two-dimensional summand by the square roots in (14). It has mean zero, identity covariance by (14), and a uniformly bounded third absolute moment because \(R_i\) is bounded and the variances in (14) are bounded away from zero. For each fixed \(t\in\mathbb R^2\), Taylor expansion with the third-order remainder therefore gives, uniformly in \(h\in H_m(\xi)\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{m,h}\exp\!\left(\frac{\mathrm i\,t^{\mathsf T}X_i(h)}{\sqrt n}\right)
 =1-\frac{\|t\|_2^2}{2n}+O(n^{-3/2}),
\]
where \(X_i(h)\) denotes that standardized summand. Raising this characteristic function to the \(n\)-th power gives \(\exp(-\|t\|_2^2/2)+o(1)\), uniformly in \(h\). A subsequence argument converts the uniform characteristic-function convergence into uniform weak convergence: otherwise a violating sequence \(h_n\) would have a subsequence in the compact set \(H_m(\xi)\), while the preceding expansion would force the Gaussian limit along that subsequence. The uniform linear expansion and variance consistency then give the asserted studentized \(\mathcal N_2(0,I_2)\) limit.

Let the unprojected signed-cell intervals be the intervals centered at \(\overline L_{n,m}\) and \(\overline U_{n,m}\) with respective half-widths \(\kappa_{\delta_0}\widehat\sigma_L/\sqrt n\) and \(\kappa_{\delta_0}\widehat\sigma_U/\sqrt n\). The uniform Gaussian limit implies that their joint coverage tends uniformly to
\[
 \{2\Phi_{\mathrm N}(\kappa_{\delta_0})-1\}^2=1-\delta_0.                  \tag{17}
\]
Both true endpoints lie in the projection ranges specified in \(\mathrm{def:signed-cell-mean-interval}\). Scalar projection of an interval onto a range containing the true value preserves containment of that value. Hence (17) proves the claimed limiting lower coverage for \(C^{\mathrm{sign}}_{n,m}\). This argument is asymptotic on the separated set and does not claim finite-sample membership of \(C^{\mathrm{sign}}_{n,m}\) in \(\mathcal I_{n,m}\), as required.
